title: From Crypto Markets to Edge AI Wearables
content:
My path into tech ran through crypto. Seven years across MEXC Global, OKX Ventures, Mindfulness Capital and FutureMoney taught me how new platforms find product-market fit, how incentives shape user behavior, and how fast "emerging" becomes "everyday".

Now, as a STEM MBA candidate at the Leavey School of Business, Santa Clara University, I'm applying that lens to edge AI wearables. The crypto thesis was simple: remove the middleman. The edge AI thesis rhymes: move intelligence off the cloud and onto the device.

On-device inference means lower latency, better privacy, and no connectivity tax — exactly what wearables need to become genuinely useful instead of notification relays. Walking around Silicon Valley, it feels like the early days of crypto: infrastructure quietly getting good while everyone waits for the interface that makes it mainstream.

I believe the teams that win will pair hardware discipline with business-model creativity — the same pairing that separated durable crypto companies from the ones that faded.

title: Multimodal Memory: What Companion Devices Should Remember
content:
Everyone is building AI companions. Very few are building AI companions that remember. Memory — across voice, vision, and text — is what turns a chatbot into a companion.

At the AWS x A10 Hack 2026, my team of four built Aide-commerce: an AI shopping agent with its own identity, every action checked, and a kill switch that refuses the agent's next request in about 0.7 seconds. Building it convinced me that trust and control matter more than raw model quality — especially for devices that share your daily life.

Multimodal memory and companion devices raise the stakes, because they see and hear everything. The questions I keep coming back to: What should be remembered? Who is allowed to replay a memory? How does a user stop the device mid-task, and how fast does it comply?

My answer, borrowed from years in crypto investment and business development: design for accountability first. Identity, auditability, and an instant off switch aren't compliance checkboxes — they are the product.
